mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 8% signals a deepening recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and UNRATE rises above 8% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one NBER-dated recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the trigger fails to fire during a documented labor market downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output that reduces corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during an NBER-identified contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one post-recession recovery window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% for six consecutive months signals a prolonged period of disinflation or deflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a documented disinflation period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion that boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not fire during a documented labor market boom.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) and the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening demand across consumption and investment channels, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a documented late-cycle expansion.
